cohort: The study included 52 apparently healthy term small for gestational age (SGA) infants and 154 appropriate for gestational age (AGA) infants from South India, recruited at birth.
finding: SGA infants had significantly lower anthropometric measurements (weight, length) at birth, 6 months, and 12 months compared to AGA infants, but their growth velocities were largely similar, with SGA infants showing significantly higher weight velocity from 9 to 12 months.
birth_weight: AGA: median 2.87 kg (2.67-3.04 kg); SGA: median 2.39 kg (2.25-2.54 kg)
